intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CDC23 gene (603462) on chromosome 5q31.2.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CDC23 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified two homozygous missense variants (c.986A > G, p.Y329C and c.988C > T, p.R330C) in CDC23 that are responsible for female infertility characterized by oocyte maturation defects
checks.explanation: Paper reports only homozygous variants; compound heterozygous mutation is not addressed in this abstract.

checks.claim: The CDC23 gene is located on chromosome 5q31.2.
checks.evidence_quote: CDC23 (cell division cycle 23) is one of the core subunits of the APC/C.
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene discussed; not stated in abstract.

paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28) is an autosomal recessive form of female infertility. Its main feature is defective oocyte maturation. Fertilization failure and early embryonic arrest have also been seen in infertile women with biallelic variants in genes encoding anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) subunits.

checks.claim: OZEMA28 is an autosomal recessive form of female infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: These APC/C gene mutations all showed a recessive inheritance pattern.
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance in female infertility stated; the term 'autosomal' and the OZEMA28 label are not used but follow from the stated pattern.

checks.claim: The main feature of OZEMA28 is defective oocyte maturation.
checks.evidence_quote: responsible for female infertility characterized by oocyte maturation defects in three infertile individuals
checks.explanation: Main feature is oocyte maturation defects.

checks.claim: Fertilization failure and early embryonic arrest have been observed in infertile women with biallelic variants in genes encoding anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) subunits.
checks.evidence_quote: Infertile females with biallelic mutations in APC/C genes are characterized by oocyte or early embryo defects.
checks.explanation: Title and purpose describe fertilization failure and early embryonic arrest in women with biallelic APC/C variants.

Across the 3 probands, the phenotypes included oocyte maturation defects, fertilization failure, and early embryonic arrest. The abstract did not say which phenotype occurred in which patient.

paragraphs.text: Cui et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in infertile women from 639 unrelated Chinese families. They identified 3 probands with biallelic variants in APC/C genes. Two probands (cases 1 and 2) carried compound heterozygous missense variants in the CDC23 gene: c.1277A-G, c.833A-G, c.182C-T, and c.301C-T. The abstract did not say how these variants were paired in each case. The third proband (case 3) carried compound heterozygous variants in the ANAPC13 gene (614484), c.6C-A and c.116_126del. The authors stated that all of these APC/C mutations showed a recessive inheritance pattern. In vitro, the CDC23 variants disrupted protein expression, whereas a missense variant in ANAPC13 was linked to abnormal localization in the cell. Structural modeling suggested that the variants might change chemical bonds with other APC/C subunits.

paragraphs.text: Fan et al. (2023) found that knockin mice homozygous for Cdc23 Y329C reproduced the patients' phenotype. Their oocytes had low levels of CDC23 and APC4 and accumulated securin and cyclin B1. Treatment with AZ3146 rescued the phenotype.
